title: Pronombres de Objeto Indirecto — Practice
description: Authored B1 practice set for indirect object pronouns: le/les with no gender agreement, the redundant 'a + persona', telling direct from indirect objects, and placement.

lessons.summary: The indirect object is the person the action is aimed at — the answer to '¿a quién?' or '¿para quién?'. In 'Doy el libro a Juan', 'el libro' is the direct object and 'a Juan' is the indirect one. The pronouns are me, te, le, nos, les. The key difference from the direct object set: 'le' and 'les' do NOT change for gender — 'le doy el regalo' works for both Juan and María; only number matters. Spanish also doubles up in a way English never does: the pronoun is normally used even when the person is already named. 'Le doy el libro a Juan' is the natural sentence; dropping the 'le' sounds wrong. That redundant 'a + persona' is also how you disambiguate 'le', which on its own could be him, her or usted: 'Le escribo a ella'. Placement follows the same rules as the direct object pronouns: in front of a conjugated verb ('Le escribo'), attached to an infinitive, gerund or affirmative command ('Voy a escribirle', 'Escríbele'), and never attached in a negative command ('No le escribas'). When an indirect and a direct pronoun meet, the indirect goes first and le/les turns into 'se': 'Le doy el libro' + 'lo' → 'Se lo doy', never 'le lo doy'.

examples.spanish: Le doy el libro a Juan.
examples.english: I give the book to Juan.
examples.note: the pronoun is used even though Juan is named

examples.spanish: Les escribo una carta a mis padres.
examples.english: I write my parents a letter.

examples.spanish: Le compré un regalo a María.
examples.note: le doesn't change for a female recipient

examples.spanish: Voy a escribirle. / Le voy a escribir.
examples.english: I'm going to write to him.

items.prompt: ___ doy el libro a Juan.
items.promptEnglish: I give the book to Juan.
items.explanation: Juan receives the book, so he's the indirect object → le. 'Lo' would replace the book itself.

items.prompt: ___ escribo una carta a mis padres.
items.promptEnglish: I write my parents a letter.
items.explanation: Plural recipient → les. 'Los' is the direct object form.

items.prompt: ___ compré un regalo a María.
items.promptEnglish: I bought María a present.
items.explanation: 'Le' does not change for gender — it's the same for María and for Juan. Only number changes it (le → les).

items.prompt: En "Le compro flores a mi madre", ¿cuál es el objeto indirecto?
items.promptEnglish: In 'Le compro flores a mi madre', which part is the indirect object?
items.explanation: The flowers are what's bought (direct object); the mother is who they're for (indirect object).

items.prompt: "Le doy el libro" — replace 'el libro' with a pronoun too: ___
items.promptEnglish: I give it to him.
items.explanation: Before lo/la/los/las, le and les always become 'se'. 'Le lo' is impossible in Spanish.

items.prompt: "Voy a escribirle" y "Le voy a escribir" — ¿cuál es correcta?
items.promptEnglish: Which is correct: 'Voy a escribirle' or 'Le voy a escribir'?
items.explanation: With an infinitive the pronoun can go in front of the verb phrase or attach to the infinitive.

items.prompt: 'Tell him the truth.' → ___ la verdad.
items.promptEnglish: Tell him the truth.
items.explanation: Affirmative command with the pronoun attached: di + le = dile.

items.prompt: A mí ___ interesa mucho la historia.
items.promptEnglish: I'm very interested in history.
items.explanation: 'A mí' is the emphatic doubling; the pronoun itself is always 'me'. Verbs like interesar and gustar take an indirect object.

items.prompt: ¿Qué ___ regalaste a tu madre? (a ella)
items.promptEnglish: What did you give your mother?
items.explanation: Singular recipient → le, regardless of gender.

items.prompt: Mis abuelos ___ mandan dinero cada mes. (a nosotros)
items.promptEnglish: My grandparents send us money every month.
items.explanation: a nosotros → nos.

items.prompt: ¿___ puedo hacer una pregunta? (a ti)
items.promptEnglish: Can I ask you a question?
items.explanation: a ti → te.

items.prompt: ___ dije la verdad a mi jefe.
items.promptEnglish: I told my boss the truth.
items.explanation: The pronoun is used even though 'a mi jefe' is right there — Spanish doubles up where English doesn't.

items.prompt: El profesor ___ explica la lección a los estudiantes.
items.promptEnglish: The teacher explains the lesson to the students.
items.explanation: Plural recipient → les.

items.prompt: No ___ digas nada a ellos todavía.
items.promptEnglish: Don't tell them anything yet.
items.explanation: Negative command: the pronoun stays in front, and 'a ellos' is plural → les.

items.prompt: ¿Me prestas tu coche? — Sí, ___ presto el coche. (a ti)
items.promptEnglish: Will you lend me your car? — Yes, I'll lend you the car.
items.explanation: a ti → te. The car is the direct object; you are the indirect one.

items.prompt: Ella ___ pidió ayuda a su hermano.
items.promptEnglish: She asked her brother for help.
items.explanation: The brother is who the request goes to → le.

items.prompt: ___ compramos un regalo a los niños.
items.promptEnglish: We bought the children a present.
items.explanation: a los niños → les.

items.prompt: ¿___ traigo un café, señor? (a usted)
items.promptEnglish: Shall I bring you a coffee, sir?
items.explanation: 'Usted' takes the third person pronoun: le.

items.prompt: Mi jefe ___ dio las gracias. (a mí)
items.promptEnglish: My boss thanked me.
items.explanation: a mí → me.

items.prompt: Replace with a pronoun: "Doy el libro a ti" → "___ doy el libro."
items.promptEnglish: I give you the book.
items.explanation: a ti → te.

items.prompt: Replace with a pronoun: "Explico la regla a los alumnos" → "___ explico la regla."
items.promptEnglish: I explain the rule to them.
items.explanation: a los alumnos → les.

items.prompt: Escribe una frase sobre un regalo que le hiciste a alguien, usando el pronombre y también la persona (por ejemplo: "Le compré flores a mi madre").
items.promptEnglish: Write a sentence about a present you gave someone, using both the pronoun and the named person (e.g. 'Le compré flores a mi madre').
items.guidance: Must contain an indirect object pronoun (me/te/le/nos/les) matching a named recipient introduced by 'a', e.g. 'Le regalé un libro a mi hermano'. The pronoun must agree in number with the recipient (le for one person, les for several) and must not be replaced by a direct object pronoun (lo/la). Mark incorrect if the pronoun is omitted entirely ('Compré flores a mi madre').
items.sampleAnswer: Le compré unas flores a mi madre por su cumpleaños.
items.explanation: Spanish keeps the indirect object pronoun even when the person is named.
